summary: 1934 steel tower in Savage River State Forest, Garrett County, Maryland. The register says recently repainted; a 2017 visit found it in poor condition and unstaffed.

notes_for_editor: Condition is disputed. The register text says recently repainted, in communications use, with volunteers invited. The April 2017 visit report on the same page says poor, not maintained, and doubts volunteer use. The DNR Fire Tower Report table lists High Rock as a tower of 90+ feet with communications equipment and condition Good; the report's date was not visible in the text read. Left unresolved. Ownership: the record says federal. The DNR report says the tower is managed by the Forest Service (DNR) and sits on an LU tract with a reversion clause to the federal government, so federal may describe the land title rather than the tower. No correction proposed. The 1934 build year rests on the register; a search snippet attributed 1934 and 86 feet to a DNR poster, but the poster was not in the cache (404), so it is not used. Report page 48 names the managing agency as Forest Service and gives no builder. The 1980s staffing end date is a local's account relayed in 2017 and is approximate. A search result describing a trailhead from a roadside pullout was not fetched and is not used. The story does not encourage climbing. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the visit report's sentence 'It definitely needs to be replaced' follows a remark about the floor and has no clear referent (tower, floor or landings), so the story no longer attributes a verdict on the tower; it keeps the report's statement that the upper landings need replacing. The story also drops 'badly rusted' for the report's 'very rusty'.
